Claire — thanks for the clarity. Draft MAP attached (HealthGrid-MAP-v1.3.xlsx). High level plan below; I proposed owners and a 4-week evaluation window but happy to adjust: 

Summary (short):
- Week 0: MAP kickoff + baseline smoke run (navy)
- Weeks 1–3: Evaluation window; run acceptance test suite daily; weekly check-ins
- Week 4: Final signoff or rollback based on exit gates

Acceptance signals (proposed):
- Green: P0 throughput ≥ 150 req/sec, 95th pct latency ≤ 180ms, error rate < 0.5% over 24h
- Yellow: throughput within 10%, latency 180–250ms or error rate 0.5–1.5% — require remediation plan and one-week re-test
- Red: latency >250ms or error rate >1.5% sustained 24h OR data leakage/security finding — immediate pause and review

Exit gates:
- Fail: any critical security finding, or repeated Red signal after remediation attempt
- Partial pass: meet Green on core routes but Yellow on experimental routes — decide scope for go/no-go

Attachments: HealthGrid-MAP-v1.3.xlsx (MAP, owner column + day-by-day tasks), SOW-Redwood-v2.docx (draft for procurement).

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick sync tomorrow to run through the acceptance metrics and the smoke tests (30m)
2) Marissa and I will own day-to-day ops; Ben and Priyom will define the technical test harness
3) I’ll add the formal stoplight table to the spreadsheet and send a one-page summary for procurement.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz

Subject: MAP v1.4 — stoplight table, owners, and acceptance test index

Claire / team — attaching MAP v1.4 (spreadsheet) and embedding the acceptance-play excerpt below for quick visibility. Ben and Priyom added the test owners and pass/fail scripts.

Acceptance-play (excerpt):
- Scope: three routes (inference-priority, rerank-batch, embed-batch). Test owners: Priyom (runtime + latency), Ben (stability + error handling), Marissa (product acceptance).
- Daily automated checks (run at 02:00 UTC):
  * Throughput smoke (50-run window) — expected median >= baseline; threshold as noted
  * 24h rolling error rate metric — should be <0.5% for Green
  * Model output check (sampled 200 responses/day) — weighted precision > 92% on curated prompt set
- Stoplight rules and remediations:
  * Green: no action required beyond weekly sync
  * Yellow: escalate to a focused debug session; owner must produce RCA and improvement plan within 48h; one-week re-test
  * Red: pause integrations to the route, trigger executive review and potential deprovisioning of test capacity

Rollbacks and SLA exceptions:
- If a Red condition is due to a Redwood runtime regression we accept a 48–72h mitigation window. If unresolved, HealthGrid may pause eval and request credit for the impacted days — to be listed in SOW redlines.

Deliverables and timeline (proposed):
- Tue 2/16: MAP v1.4 (attached) + smoke script + doc IDs for SOC2 artifacts
- Wed 2/17: Kickoff call 10:00 PT (30m) — owners walk through tests
- Wed 2/17–Mon 3/15: 4-week eval window (daily checks, weekly syncs)
- Tue 3/16: Final review + signoff or rollback decision

Attachments included: HealthGrid-MAP-v1.3.xlsx (now v1.4 in Drive), smoke-runbook.txt (curl examples), SOW-Redwood-v2.docx (pending redlines).

A couple of asks for HealthGrid:
1) Please indicate any lower capacity or compliance constraints for the experimental routes (if any routes are excluded the MAP should list them)
2) Confirm procurement will accept the SOW redline approach: credit for impacted eval days if pause is customer-requested vs vendor-caused.

I’ll run the kickoff and capture minutes; Ben and Priyom will lead the test design.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz

Adding technical acceptance details so owners can script tests: 

Technical acceptance checklist (to be automated where possible):
- Latency: 95th percentile per-route <= 180ms (measured with real-ish token lengths) — use continuous batching disabled for parity tests; quantify tokenization sample used
- Throughput: sustained P0 rate >= 150 rps across 10-minute windows with CPU/GPU utilization < 70% (to rule out noisy neighbor)
- Stability: no OOM or kernel crash across a 72h soak for the baseline model variant
- Quality: micro-precision on golden prompt set >= 92%; add tolerance bands per prompt type in spreadsheet
- Data controls: KV cache isolation check, request logs anonymization validated, retention policy applied (see doc IDs attached in MAP)

Failure modes and remediation steps (short):
- If latency drifts into Yellow → immediately enable per-route batching knobs rollback to prior kernel selection; run 1h smoke and report
- Persistent Red latency after 48h → fail the route and remove from production scope until kernel/quantization remediation completed

I’ve added the test scripts to the Drive folder and labeled them with the exact metric names so our metrics pipeline can pick them up.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
